description: Wave 8 Post-Release Performance Reliability Gates — incident shielding, threshold hardening, drift detection, and operability.

wave7_reference.note: W8 thresholds are tightened relative to W7.  W7 gates remain active as the outer hard limit.

hard_gates.description: Hardened point-read p99 must not exceed 175 µs (tightened from W7's 200 µs).
hard_gates.rationale: A 12.5% tighter gate provides early-warning margin before the W7 outer limit is reached.

hard_gates.description: Hardened write throughput must sustain ≥ 90 000 ops/s (raised from W7's 80 000).
hard_gates.rationale: A 12.5% higher throughput floor catches write-path erosion before ingest SLAs are at risk.

hard_gates.description: Hardened batch write (500 records) p99 must not exceed 4 ms (tightened from W7's 5 ms).
hard_gates.rationale: 20% tighter gate catches batch-path regression before pipeline SLAs are breached.

hard_gates.description: Concurrent write-storm scenario must sustain ≥ 60 000 ops/s across 4 writer threads.
hard_gates.rationale: Write-storm incident gate: below this rate, peak ingest cannot recover from a write-storm.

hard_gates.description: All required triage counters (mean, p99, throughput, gate_passed) must be emitted.
hard_gates.rationale: Missing triage counters make automated incident routing impossible.

hard_gates.description: At least 80% of hot paths must have a performance gate assigned.
hard_gates.rationale: Uncovered hot paths are invisible to regression detection.

soft_gates.description: Read throughput drift CV across rolling segments should stay below 8%.
soft_gates.rationale: CV > 8% on rolling windows indicates creeping degradation that requires investigation.

soft_gates.description: Write throughput drift CV across rolling segments should stay below 10%.
soft_gates.rationale: Write CV is higher due to compaction; 10% is the post-release acceptable ceiling.

soft_gates.description: Latency trend slope must not be consistently positive (rising trend = drift).
soft_gates.rationale: A sustained upward latency trend is the earliest signal of performance degradation.

soft_gates.description: Per-benchmark CV across repetitions should stay below 3% (flake noise floor).
soft_gates.rationale: High CV masks real regressions and increases false-positive rate.

soft_gates.description: Frozen baseline must not be older than 30 days.
soft_gates.rationale: A stale baseline drifts from current hardware/software reality, causing false positives.

soft_gates.description: Burst-read spike mean latency should stay below 250 µs.
soft_gates.rationale: Burst-pattern latency directly impacts SLA during traffic spikes.

soft_gates.description: Seed reproducibility must produce zero key-sequence mismatches.
All W8 threshold changes must comply with the maintenance window policy rules.
soft_gates.rationale: Loosened gates without policy approval violate the performance governance contract.

known_limitations: IRS-02 write-storm uses 4 threads (reduced from 8 in the original incident) to fit CI resource budget.
IRS-05 concurrent ingest+read background reader runs until main thread finishes; jitter on shared CI runners may cause occasional soft-gate warnings.
THD-03/04 drift detection runs kDriftSegments=6 segments per benchmark iteration; on slow CI runners each repetition may take >60 s.
DCH-06 parallel isolation benchmark uses a shared global instance counter; results must be interpreted per-fixture-instance.
ORP-07 simulates a 14-day-old baseline; in production CI the actual baseline JSON creation timestamp must be read and compared.
Drift slope values (THD-05, THD-03, THD-04) depend on steady_clock resolution; results on VMs with coarse clocks may show zero slope.
